subject: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing

Team —

Quick kickoff for the Acme private deployment handoff: during the module steward sync we discovered a mismatch between the helm egress annotations and the Terraform egress ACLs. Before the customer cutover we need a short CI runway plan that proves we can enforce and test egress at the module boundary without blocking normal traffic.

Goal: have an automated smoke + negative test in the private CI that validates 1) allowed outbound CIDR/ports, 2) graceful fallback when egress rules tighten, and 3) rollout gating that prevents promotion on regressions.

Attachments: egress-test-plan.pdf (proposal) and a small helm-values diff that shows the annotation pattern I want validated.

Asks:
- Marissa: can you validate the Helm values pattern in the staging chart today?
- Dev: can you add a pipeline job stub that runs the connectivity test against the staging VPC and fails on unexpected outbound egress? Keep it isolated to the acme-priv CI pool.
- Kim: any compliance evidence we should collect in the runbook? I want this to be easy to audit for the SOC2 evidence pack.

I'll loop in Sanjay on the CIDR ranges they need allowed. If we can get a green test by end of week we can include it in the module release checklist.

Thanks,
Jonas
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing

Jonas —

I reviewed the helm-values diff quickly. The annotation pattern is fine, but the chart templates expect a namespaced NetworkPolicy object that our current terraform module doesn't create by default. Two options: 1) add the NetworkPolicy resource to the helm chart (recommended), or 2) expose an output from Terraform that the chart can consume to set the policy.

For a quick proof we could ship a namespaced NetworkPolicy in the chart and gate it behind a feature flag (values.enabled). That will make the helm test straightforward.

I'll prototype the chart change this afternoon and attach a small test harness (kubectl + curl-based) to the egress-test-plan.

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Private Deployments
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-28T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing

Thanks — a couple of notes from Acme side:

1) CIDR/ports: please allow outbound to 54.192.0.0/12:443 for our telemetry sink and 52.94.0.0/15:443 for backups. We'll provide a finalized list by EOD.
2) We need the negative testing to simulate a tightened egress rule that blocks 0.0.0.0/0 except the allowed ranges. Can you show how the app behaves (timeouts, retries) when outbound is blocked? That is a customer ask.
3) For runbook evidence we need logs that show the test execution, the terraform plan/apply diff, and the helm release history (helm get all). PDF or archived text is fine.

We're available for a quick 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the CI job if helpful.

—Sanjay
Principal Infra Engineer, Acme Corp
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acme-corp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-28T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing

Sanjay / team —

I've sketched the CI job in the acme-priv Gitlab file (wip branch) and added two stages: 
- egress-smoke (runs a pod that attempts allowed + blocked outbound probes and records results)
- egress-tighten-sim (applies a temporary terraform change to limit egress to allowed CIDRs, then runs the app probe to capture behavior)

Important implementation notes:
- The terraform change is applied into a temporary workspace and rolled back automatically; we also capture terraform plan output to the artifacts bucket for audit.
- The Helm change is feature-flagged by values.egressPolicy.enabled so we can toggle without chart bump for other customers.
- I added artifact collection steps: helm history, terraform plan/text, and raw test logs (archived tgz).

Link to my branch and pipeline spec: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_egress-proof-plan (see folder /ci-sandbox).

I will send a merge request once Marissa confirms the NetworkPolicy template path.

—Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Infra CI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: module stewardship & CI runway — network egress proofing

All —

This plan looks good from compliance — two asks before we mark the module release-ready: 1) include a short evidence checklist in the runbook (terraform plan artifact, helm history, artifact logs) with links to the artifacts location, and 2) make sure the pipeline emits a signed timestamped artifact (we use a simple GPG sign + metadata file) so the SOC2 reviewer can validate provenance.

If Dev can wire the signing step into the artifacts job and Marissa pushes the NetworkPolicy template behind the feature flag, I am comfortable approving the module release gate. We can then add the proof artifacts to the Acme evidence bundle.

I'll mark JIRA-OPS-1247 as "compliance-ready pending MR" and follow up on the SOC2 evidence packaging.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
